<reason>CON held the marginal-deals frame throughout and PRO never closed the net-benefit gap under the motion as written. PRO's price and rivalry story is strong for 4-to-3 horizontals, but CON showed vertical double-marginalization/coordination benefits, challenger-building combos, and startup commercialization losses survive PRO's contracts-or-build-another-way reply, that blocking harm can be permanent not temporary paperwork, and that PRO's only-passed-through-efficiencies-count rule rewrites the productivity side of the motion.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's pass-through pressure (B3.1) won a concession that nothing guarantees savings reach shoppers (A4.1), but CON's reply turned it to selective enforcement and exposed PRO's weighing error, while CON's delay-cost and vertical-filter pressure left PRO minimizing permanent blocking losses.</best_rebuttal>
